Marathon Petroleum stock has fallen 1.49% over two weeks, with today's modest decline continuing a broader selloff that accelerated sharply from November 13 through November 18. The main driver is a reported shift in market sentiment: a major financial outlet published a story this past weekend saying "the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding," signaling that investors who profited heavily from high refining margins are now rotating out of the sector. Refinery stocks like Marathon have been among the market's strongest performers during periods of tight fuel supplies and high margins, so a narrative that this trade is over can trigger rapid exits.

The underlying refining picture remains reasonably solid—refineries are running at 95.7% capacity and crude inventories are moderate at 694 million barrels—but that strength may no longer be enough to hold investor attention if the belief has shifted to "this outperformance is priced in and done." Persistent Middle East tensions involving Saudi and Iranian assets also create uncertainty about future crude supply and prices, which could weigh on refiner stocks until geopolitical risks clarify.
